system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Meta-selected normaliser from simulated source episodes
SUMMARY: Simulate few-shot episodes on the source modalities, record which inductive normaliser (global CDF, residual CDF, alignment-adaptive residual CDF) works best as a function of support-measurable features (alignment rho, K, score spread), and use this rule to pick the normaliser for the unseen modality from its supports alone.
HYPOTHESIS: The meta-selected normaliser is within 0.3 AUROC points of the best normaliser in hindsight on at least five of six held-out datasets, and on average better than any single fixed normaliser.
RATIONALE: The alignment-adaptive parent blends two normalisers with one statistic. A more general principle — algorithm selection by meta-learning — chooses among several normalisers using features that can be measured on the K supports. The source modalities provide labelled episodes on which the choice can be learned, and leave-one-modality-out evaluation tests whether that choice transfers.
METHOD: 1) meta_select.py: on each source modality's validation split, 50 episodes per K; features: rho, K, coefficient of variation of LOO support scores, fraction of foreground patches; label: best normaliser by episode AUROC. 2) Fit a depth-2 decision tree on the pooled episodes of the training fold. 3) Target: compute features from the supports, choose the normaliser; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No adapter training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: each fixed normaliser; oracle choice in hindsight. Falsified if meta-selection is not better on average than the best fixed normaliser.

Idea B:
TITLE: Empirical CDF of anatomy residuals for inductive MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Subtract a shrunk position-wise median of support scores from every patch score and map the residual through one global leave-one-out empirical CDF of support residuals, then fuse with MVFA's unchanged rule.
HYPOTHESIS: Mapping position-wise residuals through a global empirical CDF matches the global empirical CDF in image AUROC (within 1 point) and improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point on aligned modalities, with lower variance across support draws at K = 2 than the position-wise CDF.
RATIONALE: This combination takes the positional part from the position-wise parent only as a location correction, and the scale from the empirical-CDF parent as a single global reference. Separating location (local, needs few values) from scale (global, needs many) avoids estimating local spreads from a handful of supports, which is the weak point of both a position-wise z-score and a local CDF at K = 2.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: positional_median(support_maps) with 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage 20; residual reference set R = {s - med_j} over all LOO support patches. 2) test_few.py: r = s_j - med_j; F(r) via searchsorted on R; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: global empirical CDF; position-wise CDF. Metric of stability: standard deviation of AUROC over support draws. Falsified if residual CDF is not more stable than the position-wise CDF at K = 2.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea B is significantly stronger because it directly addresses the core statistical challenge of low-sample inductive support normalization in MVFA by decoupling location (positional median) from scale (global empirical CDF pool). In contrast, Idea A proposes meta-learning/algorithm selection among candidate normalizers, which adds unnecessary heuristic meta-modeling complexity instead of solving the fundamental statistical estimation failure at low K.

CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=B
